title: Take the Key!
classification: photographic work; exact medium, dimensions, capture date, and technical constitution remain subject to registrar/technical verification

artist_statement.text:
Take the Key !

What lies behind the door, and who holds the key to open it?


For centuries, doors have been symbols of knowledge and power. Not everyone could access the palaces of kings, the sacred chambers of temples, and the secret archives of states. The key was given only to a select few. Because whoever held the key also decided which part of the truth would be revealed.


The light-filled door in this photograph represents the new threshold of the modern age. The person standing before the door, gazing into the unknown, is actually looking at the limits of their own freedom. The weight of the stone walls behind them symbolizes the central authorities of the past; the bright light in front symbolizes the possibility of a new world.


This is where the Web3 idea emerges. The traditional internet often consisted of doors owned by others. Our data, identities, and digital presence were hidden within grand fortresses. The keys were in the hands of platforms. Web3 asks a different question: What if the key belonged directly to the user?


This key wouldn't just open an account; it would represent the individual's digital sovereignty, ownership, and identity. For the first time, humanity approaches becoming not merely a guest, but a potential owner of the digital world.


But not every door opens to freedom. Some only lead to new labyrinths. Therefore, the most important question of Web3 is not technology, but consciousness. Holding the key also means taking responsibility. The person who opens their own door can no longer blame a gatekeeper for what they have lost.


The elongation of the shadow of the figure in the photograph within the light is no coincidence. Because a person is divided in two before every new door: one is their past self, the other is the future they do not yet know. Opening the door is not actually changing location, but transformation.


Perhaps the greatest truth of life is this: Doors are not found in the outside world, but within the person. And keys are not made of metal, but of awareness. Web3, blockchain, or digital property are merely tools. The real question is whether humanity can become the guardian of its own doors.


And in this photograph, that lonely person standing on the threshold of the light silently whispers to us:


"The future is not a door. The future is the moment you hold the key in your hand."
